subtitle: Notebooks are the lab bench of AI engineering. You prototype here, then move what works into production.

subtitle: Containers make "works on my machine" a thing of the past.

subtitle: Your editor is your co-pilot. Configure it once so it stays out of your way and starts pulling its weight.

title: Data Management
subtitle: Data is the fuel. How you manage it determines how fast you go.

title: Terminal & Shell
subtitle: The terminal is where AI engineers live. Get comfortable here.

title: Linux for AI
subtitle: Most AI runs on Linux. You need to know enough to not be stuck.

title: Debugging and Profiling
subtitle: The worst AI bugs don't crash. They train silently on garbage and report a beautiful loss curve.

title: Python for AI Engineering
subtitle: Most code in this course uses the same small set of Python idioms. Learn that set here, before the math and model lessons depend on it.

title: Linear Algebra Intuition
subtitle: Every AI model is just matrix math wearing a fancy hat.

title: Vectors, Matrices & Operations
subtitle: Every neural network is just matrix multiplication with extra steps.

title: Matrix Transformations
subtitle: A matrix is a machine that reshapes space. Learn what it does to every point, and you understand the whole transformation.

title: Calculus for Machine Learning
subtitle: Derivatives tell you which way is downhill. That is all a neural network needs to learn.

title: Chain Rule & Automatic Differentiation
subtitle: The chain rule is the engine behind every neural network that learns.

title: Probability and Distributions
subtitle: Probability is the language AI uses to express uncertainty.

title: Bayes' Theorem
subtitle: Probability is about what you expect. Bayes' theorem is about what you learn.

title: Optimization
subtitle: Training a neural network is nothing more than finding the bottom of a valley.

title: Information Theory
subtitle: Information theory measures surprise. Loss functions are built on it.

title: Dimensionality Reduction
subtitle: High-dimensional data has structure. You find it by looking from the right angle.

title: Singular Value Decomposition
subtitle: SVD is the Swiss Army knife of linear algebra. Every matrix has one. Every data scientist needs one.

title: Tensor Operations
subtitle: Tensors are the common language between data and deep learning. Every image, every sentence, every gradient flows through them.

title: Numerical Stability
subtitle: Floating point is a leaky abstraction. It will bite you during training, and you will not see it coming.

title: Norms and Distances
subtitle: Your distance function defines what "similar" means. Choose wrong and everything downstream breaks.

title: Statistics for Machine Learning
subtitle: Statistics is how you know if your model actually works or just got lucky.

title: Sampling Methods
subtitle: Sampling is how AI explores the space of possibilities.

title: Linear Systems
subtitle: Solving $Ax = b$ is the oldest problem in mathematics that still runs your neural network.

title: Convex Optimization
subtitle: Convex problems have one valley. Neural networks have millions. Knowing the difference matters.

title: Complex Numbers for AI
subtitle: The square root of -1 is not imaginary. It is the key to rotations, frequencies, and half of signal processing.

title: The Fourier Transform
subtitle: Every signal is a sum of sine waves. The Fourier transform tells you which ones.

title: Graph Theory for Machine Learning
subtitle: Graphs are the data structure of relationships. If your data has connections, you need graph theory.

title: Stochastic Processes
subtitle: Randomness with structure. The math behind random walks, Markov chains, and diffusion models.

title: What Is Machine Learning
subtitle: Machine learning is teaching computers to find patterns in data instead of writing rules by hand.

title: Linear Regression
subtitle: Linear regression draws the best straight line through your data. It is the "hello world" of machine learning.

title: Logistic Regression
subtitle: Logistic regression bends a straight line into an S-curve to answer yes-or-no questions with probabilities.

title: Decision Trees and Random Forests
subtitle: A decision tree is just a flowchart. But a forest of them is one of the most powerful tools in ML.

title: Support Vector Machines
subtitle: Find the widest street between two classes. That is the entire idea.

title: K-Nearest Neighbors and Distances
subtitle: Store everything. Predict by looking at your neighbors. The simplest algorithm that actually works.

title: Unsupervised Learning
subtitle: No labels, no teacher. The algorithm finds structure on its own.

title: Feature Engineering & Selection
subtitle: A good feature is worth a thousand data points.

title: Model Evaluation
subtitle: A model is only as good as the way you measure it.

title: Bias-Variance Tradeoff
subtitle: Every model error comes from one of three sources: bias, variance, or noise. You can only control the first two.

title: Ensemble Methods
subtitle: A group of weak learners, combined correctly, becomes a strong learner. This is not a metaphor. It is a theorem.

title: Hyperparameter Tuning
subtitle: Hyperparameters are the knobs you turn before training starts. Turning them well is the difference between a mediocre model and a great one.

title: ML Pipelines
subtitle: A model is not a product. A pipeline is. The pipeline is everything from raw data to deployed prediction, and every step must be reproducible.

title: Naive Bayes
subtitle: The "naive" assumption is wrong, and it works anyway. That's the beauty of it.

title: Time Series Fundamentals
subtitle: Past performance does predict future results -- if you check for stationarity first.

title: Anomaly Detection
subtitle: Normal is easy to define. Abnormal is whatever doesn't fit.

title: Handling Imbalanced Data
subtitle: When 99% of your data is "normal," accuracy is a lie.

title: Feature Selection
subtitle: More features is not better. The right features is better.

title: ML System Design — From Problem to Deployed Model
subtitle: A model is one part of a system. The design decides what the model predicts, who acts on it, what it costs, and what happens when it fails.

title: Monitoring Models in Production — Data Drift and Concept Drift
subtitle: A deployed model fails without an error message. It keeps returning scores while the world moves away from its training data, and only monitoring shows the gap.

title: Feature Stores and Training-Serving Skew
subtitle: A feature has one definition and two readers. Training reads its history as of each label time, and serving reads its latest value. When the two readers disagree, the model sees inputs that it never trained on.

title: The Perceptron
subtitle: The perceptron is the atom of neural networks. Split it open and you find weights, a bias, and a decision.
